documents.title: Generative AI Guidance
documents.summary: UWM-wide guidance on responsible GenAI use. It sets general principles (follow law, verify output, protect data by risk level) and sets no stance on student use in courses.
documents.stance_why: A coded delegates, B coded permit. The page sets university-wide guidelines ("the following guidelines should be adhered to when utilizing Generative AI tools": follow law, verify output, protect data by risk level) and commits UWM to giving students the skills to succeed "in an AI-driven world". It never hands the decision to instructors or courses (the pointer to the Center for Advancing Student Learning is for acceptable-use questions), so it does not delegate; it allows GenAI use under conditions, which is permit.

units.why: The intro says UWM "is committed to providing students with the knowledge, skills and experience necessary to sustain success in an AI-driven world", a career-readiness rationale for engaging with AI, so P44 (informs).
units.anchor: committed to providing students with the knowledge, skills and experience necessary
units.frag_start: The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee is committed
units.fit_note: Also carries a career-readiness rationale (P44), but it is framed as the institution's commitment, so P56 chosen.
units.resolution_why: A coded P44 (career-readiness rationale), B coded P56 (framework) with a note that it also carries P44. The source says UWM "is committed to providing students with the knowledge, skills and experience necessary to sustain success in an AI-driven world"; that is a commitment to teach students to work with AI, which P44 states; the framework role belongs to the 'guidelines' sentence (coded P116). Final P44; actor, phase, modality agree.

units.why: The opening says GenAI offers prospects for those who use it 'creatively, responsibly and ethically' but poses 'considerable dangers' without understanding the risks; this weighs benefits and risks before use, so P118.
units.anchor: it also poses considerable dangers for those who venture into the realm of Generative AI
units.frag_start: However, it also poses considerable dangers
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. The source says GenAI "poses considerable dangers for those who venture into the realm of Generative AI without a comprehensive grasp of the associated risks", a real statement weighing risks of AI use, so kept as P118 informs.

units.why: "the following guidelines should be adhered to when utilizing Generative AI tools" sets the purpose and scope of an institution-wide set of principles, so P56 (framework) rather than a specific rule type.
units.anchor: the following guidelines should be adhered to when utilizing Generative AI tools
units.frag_start: As part of the university’s commitment
units.resolution_why: A coded P56 (framework), B coded P116 (general ethical-use expectation) with unit_stance permit. The source says "As part of the university's commitment to the ethical and responsible use of Generative AI, the following guidelines should be adhered to"; it states a general expectation of ethical, responsible use (P116) and the guidelines themselves are the framework only in the document sense. Unit stance is neutral because the sentence does not itself permit anything. Actor, phase, modality agree.

units.why: "Do not use the tools in an unethical way or as part of any illegal activity" and comply with acceptable use policies: a duty to follow law and existing university policy, so P77.
units.anchor: Do not use the tools in an unethical way or as part of any illegal
units.frag_start: Do not use the tools
units.fit_note: Also bans unethical use (P74 aspect); P77 chosen because the passage sits under the heading 'Follow existing laws and policies' and pairs with illegal activity.
units.resolution_why: A coded P77, B coded P74 with unit_stance prohibit. The source says "Do not use the tools in an unethical way or as part of any illegal activity" under the heading "Follow existing laws and policies"; the legal frame makes P77 the place a reader would look, and the 'unethical' clause is noted in fit_note. P74 targets deceptive, fabricated or malicious use, which the passage does not name. Unit stance neutral (no AI use is banned as such).

units.why: It requires compliance with hosting entities' acceptable use policies and names Universities of Wisconsin policies (Acceptable Use, Data Classification, Privacy), so P77.
units.anchor: Ensure compliance with acceptable use policies of any entity that hosts Generative AI tools.
units.frag_start: Ensure compliance with acceptable use policies
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this separate sentence, "Ensure compliance with acceptable use policies of any entity that hosts Generative AI tools." It is a real, distinct duty (A folded it into its P77 unit), so kept as P77.

units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. The source says GenAI "will completely make up citations, quotations, and descriptions", a factual statement supporting the verify-output rule, so kept as P31 informs.

documents.title: Syllabus Statements: Guiding Student Generative AI Usage in Your Class
tiers: Allowing the full use of Generative AI
documents.summary: CASL page with a course checklist and three sample syllabus statements (full use, specific use, prohibition) plus citation and misconduct language. Instructors choose which to adopt.
documents.stance_why: It offers three sample statements ("Allowing the Full Use", "Allowing Specific AI Use", "Prohibiting AI Use") and tells each instructor to "Explicitly state your expectations", so the page itself takes no single stance and delegates.

units.why: "Explicitly state your expectations for student Generative AI use in the syllabus" is a checklist duty for each course, P09.
units.anchor: Explicitly state your expectations for student Generative AI use in the syllabus.
units.frag_start: Explicitly state your expectations
units.resolution_why: Types agree (P09). A coded course-start, B before-course. The checklist item "Explicitly state your expectations for student Generative AI use in the syllabus" is about communicating expectations to students, so course-start.

units.why: Instructors "talk directly with students about your Generative AI policy, sharing examples of what is and is not appropriate use", going beyond listing the rule, so P66.
units.anchor: talk directly with students about your Generative AI policy
units.frag_start: Include written expectations for Generative AI use
units.fit_note: Also requires written expectations on assignments, a P09-like element.
units.resolution_why: Types agree (P66). A coded should, B coded must. The checklist opens "For each class, be sure to:" and the item says "talk directly with students about your Generative AI policy", an imperative, so must (same as the neighbouring checklist item).

units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors: supply citation expectations, not the student duty itself. | Directs instructors to explain citation expectations; the disclosure rule itself binds students.

units.policy: Generative AI used to assist in assignment completion, in part (e.g., generating ideas, brainstorming, summarizing information) or in whole (e.g., submitting direct text from a Generative AI source), is not allowed in this class.

units.resolution_why: A coded P105 (ban on summarizing sources), B coded P19 (do not have AI produce submitted work). The source bans AI that assists "in part (e.g., generating ideas, brainstorming, summarizing information) or in whole (e.g., submitting direct text)"; the rule is about AI helping produce the submitted assignment, which P19 states. P105 covers only reading and summarizing sources and would drop the 'in whole' part. Both fit partly, so P19 with the fit_note. Modality must-not and phase during-work agree.
